description: Hand-labeled dataset for the Keeper's register (mood) classifier. Registers are an original construct (frozen = stuck/low/cold, tidal = moving/returning/better, turn = the rare strong lift, neutral = no mood signal -> abstain). Labels are subjective and authored by one person; treat as a directional benchmark, not ground truth. Held-out 'test' split is never used to tune thresholds. Optional external validation: map a public emotion set (e.g. dair-ai/emotion: sadness/fear -> frozen, joy/love -> tidal) for volume. Neutral coverage extended with the app's own documented tool phrasings (FEATURES.md 'Try:' lines): the original set had short generic queries but none of the search / fetch / file / git / run_python / journal shapes that dominate real traffic. Extended again with 31 REAL user messages replayed out of live sessions by backend/replay_register.py, reviewed one at a time before merging: hand-written cases only ever contain the messages you thought to invent, and this set had scored the neutral tag at 100% for every method while the live Keeper was reading 'look up watercolor brands' as frozen. One replayed message was held back at review as a real personal disclosure rather than a test phrase; the reviewing step exists for exactly that. The merge moves the majority-class baseline from 29% to 42%, so read raw accuracy against that floor and trust the per-tag columns.
